**Chad Hazlett** · Summer Institute in Computational Social Science (SICSS) 2026, UCLA

A talk on causal identification: why credible causal claims rest on assumptions that
cannot be checked in the data; how the main identification strategies (experiments,
conditional ignorability, RDD/ITS, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables,
and learning from prior outcomes) each carry their own demanding assumptions; and how
sensitivity analysis and partial identification --- "safe inference" --- let us state
honestly what we can and cannot conclude.
